title: Belt Drive Assembly
model_title: V-Belt Drive Assembly (3 Belts, Motor on Tensioning Slide Base)

introduction.definition: A V-belt drive transmits power between parallel shafts by friction between wedge-shaped belts and grooved sheaves. The speed ratio is the ratio of the sheave pitch diameters. Correct tension and alignment give long belt life.
key_points: Tension: not too slack (slip), not too tight (bearings)
Replace belts as a matched set
introduction.summary: A V-belt drive transmits power between parallel shafts by friction between wedge-shaped belts and grooved sheaves. The speed ratio equals the ratio of sheave diameters (here 2.5:1). Belts are tensioned by sliding the motor on its base; a guard protects people. Belt drives are simple, quiet, absorb shock and allow speed changes by changing sheaves.

foundation: Mount driver and driven machines on a rigid common base so centre distances and alignment stay fixed.
alignment: Align shafts parallel and the wheels/hubs in the same plane (straight-edge or laser); misalignment is the main cause of early wear.
piping: Fit guards that fully enclose moving parts but allow inspection and lubrication.
commissioning: Tension by the deflection method (force for a given deflection per span); re-tension after the first 24 h.

overhaul.task: Replace belts as a set; check groove wear.

lubrication: No belt dressing; grease plummer blocks per schedule.

A V-belt drive transmits power between parallel shafts by friction between wedge-shaped belts and grooved sheaves.
The speed ratio is the ratio of the sheave pitch diameters.

video_tutorials.title: Belt Drive Assembly — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Belt Drive Assembly.
Look/listen for slip, cracking, squeal.
Check tension and alignment.
Replace belts as a set; check groove wear.
Watch for belt slip: squeal, glazing, heat. Common cause: low tension, worn grooves, overload.
Watch for rapid belt wear: frayed sides. Common cause: misalignment.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
